method: Each listed item was read with its stem, all options, keyed answer(s), explanations and takeaway. Statuses are manually reasoned, not inferred from a schema or automated pass rule.
limitations: Independent AI editorial/clinical-reasoning screen; not external clinician validation or psychometric validation.
Pass applies only to the recorded content hash. New or changed content requires further review.
No comparison against proprietary examination items; originality judged from author provenance and item content.
Cross-bank learning-objective overlap remains provisional until all batches are available.
Source checks below support only the explicitly associated claims; other category references are general reading unless specifically verified.

sourceChecks.note: Diabetes Canada resource retrieved during legacy review: reduced-sensation foot protection and avoidance of heat injury; not a local nail-care credential audit.

Current standard opened during legacy review; consent, choice and individual preferences support these care decisions. Other routine hygiene details were reasoned, not externally verified item by item.

items.assessment: Correct cushioning concept, but deep unlined sink/empty hard basin are duplicate distractors; choice variety and clinical usefulness are limited.
issues: Correct cushioning concept, but deep unlined sink/empty hard basin are duplicate distractors; choice variety and clinical usefulness are limited.

options: Run hot water over the dentures to make them easier to grip
Hold the dentures high above a towel-lined basin for better visibility
Line the basin with a towel
Use an empty hard basin
why: Hot water can damage denture materials and does not protect against impact.
A greater drop height adds avoidable risk; work close over a protected basin.
Padding cushions fragile dentures if dropped.
A hard surface can fracture dropped dentures.

items.assessment: Painful chewing warrants oral/fit assessment before adhesive or a menu change; these are plausible common workarounds. No competing best initial answer identified.
Soft-brush mechanical cleaning is appropriate when tolerated; mouthwash-only and swab-only care are plausible insufficient substitutes. No automatic contraindication supplied.
Key merely says to follow an unspecified ordered plan, so no usable oral-care technique is assessed.
issues: Key merely says to follow an unspecified ordered plan, so no usable oral-care technique is assessed.

options: Use a standard firm-bristle brush to clear deposits
Start flossing despite no established flossing routine
Replace all cleaning with an alcohol-containing rinse
Use the prescribed soft brush with light pressure and monitor for increased bleeding
why: Firm bristles may increase trauma to fragile bleeding gums.
Introducing potentially traumatic flossing requires review with the individualized plan.
Rinsing alone inadequately removes plaque and alcohol may irritate fragile tissues.
Gentle mechanical cleaning according to the individualized bleeding-risk plan limits further trauma.
proposedChanges.stem: A client has fragile gums that bleed with firm brushing. The oral-care plan permits a soft toothbrush with light pressure and requires reporting worsening bleeding. Which approach best follows this plan?

items.assessment: Labelled dedicated storage is the clear safest alternative to common accidental-disposal locations. Simple but useful basic-care objective.
Lip moisturizer targets cracked lips; irritating alcohol/acid and a mouth rinse alone do not. Foundation-level item; swallowing status adds little to this lip-care decision.
Client declined an inconvenient time, not hygiene; finding a feasible preferred time supports autonomy. Competing morning rescheduling/family persuasion do not resolve that preference.
The key is sound, but the yesterday-safe-water option is conspicuously irrelevant and contains a missing possessive. Use a realistic unsafe testing habit.
issues: The key is sound, but the yesterday-safe-water option is conspicuously irrelevant and contains a missing possessive. Use a realistic unsafe testing habit.

options: Judge temperature with the numb foot
Rely on the usual tap setting without testing
Ask the client to keep the numb foot in the water briefly to test comfort
Check water with an intact-sensation area or thermometer
why: The affected foot may not detect a burn risk.
Tap settings do not reliably establish the final water temperature.
Reduced sensation makes foot discomfort an unreliable protection against burns.
Impaired sensation can prevent recognition of excessive heat.

items.assessment: Gentle cleansing and barrier use after incontinence are appropriate; barrier over visible urine and repeated detergent washing are plausible mistakes. No competing keyed response found.
All three distractors leave the foreskin retracted, duplicating the same error. Make this a purposeful post-care safety check with distinct wrong actions.
issues: All three distractors leave the foreskin retracted, duplicating the same error. Make this a purposeful post-care safety check with distinct wrong actions.

options: Check urine colour and postpone examining the foreskin until the next care round
Return the foreskin to its usual position
Leave the foreskin retracted because the glans is still moist
Apply more cleansing solution to avoid touching the foreskin again
why: Urine appearance does not establish that the foreskin was safely returned after care.
A retracted foreskin can constrict the glans.
Return it promptly after gentle hygiene; prolonged retraction risks constriction.
Additional cleanser does not replace restoring the normal foreskin position.

items.assessment: Options1 and2 repeat reusing contaminated material; replace one with a distinct clinically plausible technique error.
issues: Options1 and2 repeat reusing contaminated material; replace one with a distinct clinically plausible technique error.

options: Use gentle wipes with a clean surface each pass
Use one damp pad until both eyes appear clean
Apply firm pressure over the closed lids to lift the crusts quickly
Start wiping before moistening adherent crusts
why: Fresh wiping surfaces limit transfer of debris.
Reusing contaminated material can transfer secretions between surfaces.
Pressure and vigorous rubbing can injure delicate tissues; soften and wipe gently.
Moistening helps release crusts with less traction on delicate tissue.

items.assessment: Device-specific instructions appropriately outrank immersion, universal solvents and another model’s procedure. No broad nursing-scope claim is made.
Missing glasses create an observable correctable sensory barrier; offering them before cognitive labeling or taking over feeding preserves function. Continue assessment if difficulty persists.
Stem names the exact correct tool, making the key a repetition. Remove that cue and test the safe adaptation.
issues: Stem names the exact correct tool, making the key a repetition. Remove that cue and test the safe adaptation.

options: Use fragranced aftershave to cool the skin
Use the electric razor gently
Use the disposable wet razor available on the unit
Shave against hair growth to reduce repeat sessions
why: Fragrance and alcohol can irritate vulnerable skin.
This follows the plan while reducing skin cuts.
Substituting the readily available razor disregards the individualized skin plan.
A closer shave may increase irritation in fragile skin.
proposedChanges.stem: A client taking an anticoagulant has fragile facial skin and wants help shaving. An electric razor is available and suitable under the care plan. Which action best reduces skin trauma?

items.assessment: Complex nail curvature plus reduced sensation reasonably requires qualified foot-care assessment; routine ward clipping, filing to pain and soaking are plausible unsafe shortcuts. Local scope still applies.
An unscented emollient is appropriate for uncomplicated post-bath xerosis; hot prolonged bathing, extra soap and unfamiliar fragrance are credible aggravators.
Drying and inspecting a persistently moist fold addresses cause and permits skin assessment. Occlusive/unassessed products or a retained towel may worsen moisture.
The two negatives are obvious violations and option3 does not say the questions are unnecessary. Make the mistaken privacy/control responses precise.
issues: The two negatives are obvious violations and option3 does not say the questions are unnecessary. Make the mistaken privacy/control responses precise.

options: Continue the usual care sequence without asking whether the client wants to clean an accessible area
Explain each step before touch
Expose only the area being cleaned
Leave the perineum exposed while gathering supplies so cleaning can begin quickly
why: Offering feasible participation can preserve control and dignity.
Predictability supports comfort and participation.
Limited exposure protects warmth and dignity.
Gather supplies first and limit exposure to what is needed during care.

items.assessment: Supports alignment and bedding protection for an agreed feasible task; neck-support and tolerance errors are meaningful alternatives. No special contraindication in stem.

Removing uncomfortable contacts appropriately permits eye assessment; mere lubrication, postponement or covering the eyes leaves the irritant. Persistent pain/redness/vision change should trigger further urgent eye review; the item does not claim removal completes assessment.
The abnormal oral findings are valid, but denture removal is an action rather than an assessment finding. Replace it with a normal oral finding of the same type.
issues: The abnormal oral findings are valid, but denture removal is an action rather than an assessment finding. Replace it with a normal oral finding of the same type.

options: Moist pink mucosa without pain
Intact mucosa beneath a well-fitting denture with no reported pain
New white patches with mouth soreness
A new ulcer limiting eating
why: This is a reassuring oral finding.
This is a reassuring finding, unlike new painful lesions.
These may indicate a treatable oral condition.
Painful tissue injury can reduce nutritional intake.

items.assessment: A pause and jointly prioritized hygiene responds to fatigue; switching caregivers does not reduce the client’s exertion. No concerning physiological symptom requires another priority in this stable stem.
Outer-ear care and assessment of blockage avoid canal trauma. Unscreened irrigation or drops are credible mistakes, especially when pain, drainage or surgery history may contraindicate them.
Slow supported adhesive release protects fragile skin; upward pull, counter-pulling skin and abrasive residue removal are plausible errors. Specific adhesive-remover choice remains product dependent.
The supplier-name option is unrelated to effective assistance. Replace it with a relevant but insufficient process outcome.
issues: The supplier-name option is unrelated to effective assistance. Replace it with a relevant but insufficient process outcome.

options: The client can grip the adapted handle but still needs the nurse to do the brushing
The client finishes despite increased hand pain
The client completes brushing comfortably
The nurse finishes faster alone
why: Grip alone does not establish the intended comfortable self-care performance.
Completion with increased pain suggests the adaptation needs adjustment.
Adaptive support achieved the self-care goal.
Speed alone does not measure client independence.
